proof_summary: Assuming the first claimed identity, the shifted values \(Y_k=a(3773+k)+1\) obey the Fibonacci recurrence; a modular matrix computation with \(p=195318521017\) and \(j=249580073232\) gives \(Y_j\equiv0\) and \(Y_{j+1}\equiv1\pmod p\), forcing both \(a_{3774+j}\) and \(a_{3775+j}\) to be divisible by \(p\). Their gcd is therefore at least \(2\), so the defining recurrence makes the next term strictly smaller than \(1+a_{3775+j}+a_{3774+j}\), contradicting the asserted identity.
